reasons: Deviation classification is correct on the substance: Section 3.4 gives Customer a convenience right (~one month's notice) and IBM has no convenience right, but subsection (b) conditions exit on open-ended early termination charges cross-referenced to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments, with no pro-rata refund — short of the preferred penalty-free exit with refund.

Redline is targeted and actionable: it replaces only the offending payment condition in p0046 with (i) payment of charges accrued through the termination date, (ii) an express bar on early termination charges/penalties, and (iii) a 30-day pro-rata refund of prepaid charges. It correctly leaves the existing notice mechanics in p0044–p0045 alone rather than duplicating a convenience right.

Failed deterministic checks are explained by the fact pattern, not by a defect: the 'Customer convenience termination present' regex misses because the right already exists in p0044 (no need to insert model language), and the 0.824 changed-character ratio reflects the fact that the whole point of the edit is to substitute the early-termination-charge obligation, which cannot be achieved with a smaller edit.
Comment is accurate, in-voice, cites the playbook position, and offers the fallback (3 months' charges cap) consistent with the rule's fallback tier.

Minor, non-blocking gap: the redline does not address the 'end of any calendar month' timing restriction in p0044, which can push an exit slightly beyond 30 days; worth flagging in the comment but it does not undermine the edit.
